questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the following reaction, condition 'A' is -
questions.solution:
The given reaction shows the conversion of phenol to $p$-benzoquinone.

This transformation is an oxidation reaction. Phenol is oxidized to $p$-benzoquinone by strong oxidizing agents such as chromic acid ($\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ with $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ or $\text{CrO}_3$).

In contrast, reduction with zinc dust converts phenol to benzene, and $\text{CS}_2$ at low temperature is used as a solvent for monohalogenation of phenol.

Hence, condition 'A' is oxidation with $\text{CrO}_3$.

Answer: Oxidation with $\text{CrO}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alcohols contains the hydroxy group, at the side chain of the aromatic ring?
questions.solution:
Aromatic alcohols are compounds in which the hydroxyl group ($-OH$) is attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom of the side chain of an aromatic ring.

For example, benzyl alcohol ($C_6H_5CH_2OH$) is an aromatic alcohol.

If the hydroxyl group is directly attached to the aromatic ring, the compound is classified as a phenol rather than an alcohol.

Thus, aromatic alcohols contain the hydroxy group at the side chain of the aromatic ring.

Answer: aromatic alcohols

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions is preferentially used to prepare the corresponding paraffins from alkanone?
questions.solution:
Alkanones (ketones) are reduced to the corresponding paraffins (alkanes) by Clemmensen reduction. In this reaction, the carbonyl group ($ \gt C=O$) is converted into a methylene group ($ \gt CH_2$) using zinc amalgam ($Zn-Hg$) and concentrated hydrochloric acid ($HCl$).

Etard reaction is used to oxidize toluene to benzaldehyde.

Rosenmund reduction is used to convert acid chlorides into aldehydes.

Haloform reaction is used to convert methyl ketones into a haloform and a carboxylic acid salt.

Answer: Clemmensen reduction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds exhibits Schiff test?
questions.solution:
Schiff's reagent is a dilute solution of rosaniline hydrochloride (magenta dye) whose pink colour has been discharged by passing $SO_2$.

When an aldehyde is treated with Schiff's reagent, the pink or magenta colour is restored.

Ketones, carboxylic acids, and ethers do not respond to this test.

Therefore, aldehydes exhibit the Schiff test.

Answer: Aldehydes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagent used to distinguish primary and secondary amines by Hinsberg test.
questions.solution:
Hinsberg test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary amines.

The reagent used in this test is benzenesulfonyl chloride, which has the chemical formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}$.

Primary amines react with Hinsberg reagent to form an N-alkylbenzenesulfonamide, which is soluble in alkali due to the presence of an acidic hydrogen attached to nitrogen.

Secondary amines react to form an N,N-dialkylbenzenesulfonamide, which is insoluble in alkali as it lacks an acidic hydrogen.

Tertiary amines do not react with Hinsberg reagent.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aniline on treatment with $\text{NaNO}_2$ / HCl at about $0^\circ\text{C}$ gives a compound A, which on further treatment with CuCN / KCN gives a compound B, which when reacts with $\text{H}_2$ / Ni gives a compound C. The compound C on reaction with $\text{HNO}_2$ gives a compound D. The structure of D is:
questions.solution:
Aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$) undergoes diazotization with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and HCl at $0^\circ\text{C}$ to form benzene diazonium chloride (A).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl}, 0^\circ\text{C}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$ (A)

Benzene diazonium chloride reacts with CuCN / KCN to form benzonitrile (B) via the Sandmeyer reaction.

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{CuCN} / \text{KCN}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN}$ (B)

Benzonitrile is reduced by $\text{H}_2$ / Ni to form benzylamine (C).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2 / \text{Ni}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (C)

Benzylamine, being an aliphatic primary amine, reacts with nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$) to form benzyl alcohol (D) with the evolution of nitrogen gas.

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_2} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (D)

Therefore, the structure of D is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CH}_2\text{-OH}$.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CH}_2\text{-OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of compound the Legumelin is?
questions.solution:
Legumelin is a type of albumin protein found in the seeds of leguminous plants.

Albumins are water-soluble proteins that are spherical or globular in shape.

Therefore, legumelin is classified as a globular protein.

Answer: Globular protein

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product when glucose reacts with bromine water.
questions.solution:
Bromine water is a mild oxidizing agent.

When glucose reacts with bromine water, the aldehyde group ($-CHO$) is oxidized to a carboxylic acid group ($-COOH$), while the hydroxyl groups remain unaffected.

The reaction is given by:

$CHO-(CHOH)_4-CH_2OH + Br_2/H_2O \rightarrow COOH-(CHOH)_4-CH_2OH$

The product formed is gluconic acid.

Answer: Gluconic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reason for the highest boiling point of R-COOH as compared to alkanes, ethers, alcohols and aldehydes.
options: Van der waals force of attraction
questions.solution:
Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than alkanes, ethers, alcohols, and aldehydes of comparable molecular mass.

This is due to the presence of strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding in carboxylic acids. The highly polarized O-H bond, enhanced by the electron-withdrawing carbonyl group, allows carboxylic acid molecules to form strong hydrogen bonds with each other. Because of this extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding, they often exist as dimers even in the vapor phase or in non-polar solvents, requiring more energy to separate the molecules during boiling.

Answer: Formation of intermolecular hydrogen bonding

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the proportionality between (I) Bond length and size of atom (II) Bond length and multiplicity of bond respectively?
questions.solution:
Bond length is the equilibrium distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms in a molecule.

As the size of the bonded atoms increases, the distance between their nuclei increases. Thus, bond length is directly proportional to the size of the atom.

Bond multiplicity refers to the number of bonds between two atoms (single, double, triple). As bond multiplicity increases, the bond becomes stronger and the atoms are pulled closer together, decreasing the bond length. Thus, bond length is inversely proportional to the multiplicity of the bond.

Hence, (I) is direct and (II) is inverse.

Answer: (I)- direct (II)- inverse

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the order and molecularity of the following elementary reaction?
$2\text{NO}_{2(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_{(g)} + \text{O}_{2(g)}$, rate $= k \times [\text{NO}_2]^2$
options: The reaction is second order and biomolecular.
The reaction is first order and bimolecular.
The reaction is second order and unimolecular.
The reaction is zero order and unimolecular.
questions.solution:
For an elementary reaction, the rate law is determined by its stoichiometry.

Given rate $= k[\text{NO}_2]^2$

The order of the reaction is the sum of the exponents of the concentration terms in the rate law. Here, the exponent is $2$, so the order is $2$.

The molecularity of an elementary reaction is the number of reactant molecules participating in the reaction. Since $2$ molecules of $\text{NO}_2$ are reacting, the molecularity is $2$ (bimolecular).

Thus, the reaction is second order and bimolecular.

Answer: The reaction is second order and biomolecular.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the rate constant of first order reaction $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B}$ having rate $5.4 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$ and $[\text{A}] = 0.3$ M.
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the rate law is given by:

$\text{Rate} = k[\text{A}]$

Substituting the given values:

$5.4 \times 10^{-6} = k \times 0.3$

$k = \dfrac{5.4 \times 10^{-6}}{0.3}$

$k = 18 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{s}^{-1}$

$k = 1.80 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{s}^{-1}$

Answer: $1.80 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{s}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the role of catalyst in reaction?
options: To increase activation energy of a reaction
To decrease the equilibrium constant of the reaction
To supply energy to the reactants
To decrease activation energy of a reaction
questions.solution:
A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway that has a lower activation energy.

It does not alter the equilibrium constant, nor does it supply energy to the reactants.

Therefore, the primary role of a catalyst is to decrease the activation energy of a reaction.

Answer: To decrease activation energy of a reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical name of Aspirin?
questions.solution:
Aspirin is prepared by the acetylation of salicylic acid using acetic anhydride in the presence of an acid catalyst.

The chemical name of Aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid (or 2-acetoxybenzoic acid).

Answer: acetyl salicylic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following coordinate complexes is heteroleptic?
questions.solution:
A homoleptic complex has only one type of ligand attached to the central metal atom or ion.

A heteroleptic complex has more than one type of ligand attached to the central metal atom or ion.

Pentacarbonyliron(0) is $[Fe(CO)_5]$, which has only $CO$ ligands (homoleptic).

Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) is $[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]$, which has two different types of ligands, $NH_3$ and $NO_2^{-}$ (heteroleptic).

Tetraamminecopper(II) ion is $[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$, which has only $NH_3$ ligands (homoleptic).

Tetracyanonickelate(II) ion is $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$, which has only $CN^{-}$ ligands (homoleptic).

Thus, Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) is the heteroleptic complex.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following complex is neutral?
questions.solution:
A neutral complex is a coordination compound that does not have an overall electrical charge and does not dissociate into ions in solution.

$\text{K}_3[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]$ is an ionic complex that dissociates into $3\text{K}^+$ and $[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]^{3-}$ ions.

$[\text{Zn(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ is a cationic complex with a $+2$ charge.

$[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+}$ is a cationic complex with a $+2$ charge.

$[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$ has no overall charge and no counter ions, making it a neutral complex.

Answer: $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following prediction is correct when the transition metal ion is colourless?
questions.solution:
The colour of transition metal ions is primarily due to d-d transitions, which require the presence of partially filled d-orbitals.

When the d-orbitals are completely empty ($d^0$ configuration, e.g., $Sc^{3+}$, $Ti^{4+}$) or completely filled ($d^{10}$ configuration, e.g., $Zn^{2+}$, $Cu^+$), d-d transitions are not possible.

In both $d^0$ and $d^{10}$ configurations, there are no unpaired electrons. Therefore, a transition metal ion is colourless when it contains 0 unpaired electrons.

Answer: it contains 0 unpaired electrons

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of elements does NOT include transition elements?
questions.solution:
Transition elements are the d-block elements (groups 3 to 12) in the periodic table, which have incompletely filled d-orbitals in their ground state or in any of their common oxidation states.

Mn (Manganese, Group 7) and Ag (Silver, Group 11) are transition elements.

Zr (Zirconium, Group 4) and Au (Gold, Group 11) are transition elements.

Mo (Molybdenum, Group 6) and Pt (Platinum, Group 10) are transition elements.

Sn (Tin) belongs to Group 14 and is a p-block element. Pm (Promethium) is a lanthanide and belongs to the f-block. Neither of them is a transition element.

Therefore, the pair Sn and Pm does not include transition elements.

Answer: Sn and Pm

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following expressions indicates the correct relationship between molar conductivity of strong electrolyte and its concentration?
questions.solution:
The relationship between molar conductivity ($\Lambda$) and concentration ($c$) for a strong electrolyte is given by the Debye-Huckel-Onsager equation.

The equation is $\Lambda = \Lambda_0 - a\sqrt{c}$, where $\Lambda_0$ is the limiting molar conductivity at infinite dilution and $a$ is a constant that depends on the nature of the electrolyte, solvent, and temperature.

Answer: $\Lambda = \Lambda_0 - a\sqrt{c}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If molar conductance at infinite dilution for $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$ and $\text{H}^+$ ions are $50\ \text{S cm}^2\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ and $350\ \text{S cm}^2\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ respectively, molar conductivity of $5 \times 10^{-2}$ M $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is $20\ \text{S cm}^2\text{mol}^{-1}$. What is the hydrogen ion concentration in $\text{mol/dm}^3$ of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$?
questions.solution:
Molar conductivity at infinite dilution for $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is given by Kohlrausch's law:

$\Lambda_m^\infty = \lambda^\infty(\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-) + \lambda^\infty(\text{H}^+)$

$\Lambda_m^\infty = 50 + 350 = 400\ \text{S cm}^2\ \text{mol}^{-1}$

Degree of dissociation $\alpha$ is:

$\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\infty} = \dfrac{20}{400} = 0.05$

Hydrogen ion concentration is:

$[\text{H}^+] = C\alpha = (5 \times 10^{-2}) \times 0.05 = 2.5 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{mol/dm}^3$

Answer: $2.5 \times 10^{-3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Determine the electrode potential of $\text{Sn}^{2+}(0.01\text{M})\ |\ \text{Sn(s)}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ if $E^\circ_{\text{Sn}}$ is $-0.136$ V.
questions.solution:
The reduction half-reaction is $\text{Sn}^{2+} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Sn(s)}$.

Using the Nernst equation:

$E = E^{\circ} - \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log \dfrac{1}{[\text{Sn}^{2+}]}$

Substituting the given values ($n = 2$, $[\text{Sn}^{2+}] = 0.01\text{ M}$, $E^{\circ} = -0.136\text{ V}$):

$E = -0.136 - \dfrac{0.0591}{2} \log \dfrac{1}{0.01}$

$E = -0.136 - 0.02955 \log (100)$

$E = -0.136 - 0.02955 \times 2$

$E = -0.136 - 0.0591$

$E = -0.1951\text{ V} \approx -0.195\text{ V}$

Answer: $-0.195$ V

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following series contains only electrophiles?
questions.solution:
Electrophiles are electron-deficient species that can accept an electron pair. They are either positively charged or neutral molecules with an incomplete octet or highly polar bonds.

In the first series, $\text{R-OH}$ and $\text{NH}_3$ have lone pairs on oxygen and nitrogen respectively, making them nucleophiles.

In the second series, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{R}_2\text{N}^-$ have lone pairs and a negative charge respectively, making them nucleophiles.

In the third series, $\text{BF}_3$ is an electron-deficient Lewis acid with an incomplete octet. $\text{SO}_3$ has a highly electron-deficient sulfur atom due to three electronegative oxygen atoms. $\text{NO}^+$ is a positively charged ion. All three are electrophiles.

In the fourth series, $\text{R-NH}_2$ has a lone pair on nitrogen, making it a nucleophile.

Answer: $\text{BF}_3, \text{SO}_3, \text{NO}^+$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecule has Chiral Carbon?
questions.solution:
A chiral carbon atom is one that is bonded to four different atoms or groups.

Let us examine each option:
In the first molecule, the central carbon is bonded to two identical hydrogen (H) atoms. Thus, it is achiral.
In the second molecule, the central carbon is bonded to four different groups: H, CH_3$, OH, and I. Thus, it is a chiral carbon. \\ In the third molecule, the central carbon is bonded to two identical methyl (CH_3$) groups. Thus, it is achiral.
In the fourth molecule, the central carbon is bonded to two identical ethyl (C_2$H_5$) groups. Thus, it is achiral.

Therefore, only the second molecule contains a chiral carbon.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The IUPAC name of the following compound is,
questions.solution:
The parent ring in the given structure is cyclohexane.

The substituents attached to the ring are one methoxy group ($-OCH_3$) and two ethyl groups ($-CH_2CH_3$).

According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the ring must be numbered to give the lowest possible set of locants for the substituents.

If we start numbering from the carbon with the two ethyl groups, the locant set is $1, 1, 4$.

If we start numbering from the carbon with the methoxy group, the locant set is $1, 4, 4$.

Comparing the two sets, $(1, 1, 4)$ is lower than $(1, 4, 4)$ at the first point of difference. Therefore, the carbon with the two ethyl groups is designated as position $1$, and the carbon with the methoxy group is position $4$.

When writing the name, substituents are listed in alphabetical order. 'Ethyl' comes before 'methoxy' (multiplying prefixes like 'di' are ignored for alphabetization).

Thus, the correct IUPAC name is 1,1-diethyl-4-methoxycyclohexane.

Answer: 1, 1 - diethyl - 4 - methoxycyclohexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In Finkelstein reaction, which one of the following reagents is used?
questions.solution:
The Finkelstein reaction is a halogen exchange reaction used for the synthesis of alkyl iodides from alkyl chlorides or alkyl bromides.

The reaction involves treating an alkyl chloride or bromide with sodium iodide (NaI) in dry acetone.

$R-X + NaI \xrightarrow{\text{dry acetone}} R-I + NaX \downarrow$

where $X = Cl, Br$.

Sodium iodide is soluble in dry acetone, whereas sodium chloride and sodium bromide are insoluble and precipitate out. This precipitation drives the forward reaction according to Le Chatelier's principle.

Answer: NaI in dry acetone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the major product formed when 2-bromopentane reacts with alcoholic KOH?
questions.solution:
Reaction of 2-bromopentane with alcoholic KOH undergoes dehydrohalogenation (E2 elimination).

$CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3 \xrightarrow{alc. KOH, \Delta} CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2-CH_3 + CH_2=CH-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$

According to Zaitsev's rule, the more substituted alkene is formed as the major product.

Pent-2-ene is a disubstituted alkene, whereas pent-1-ene is a monosubstituted alkene.

Thus, pent-2-ene is the major product.

Answer: Pent-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reaction steps is known as propagation step
questions.solution:
In a free radical substitution reaction, the mechanism involves three types of steps:

1. Initiation step: A neutral molecule breaks down to form free radicals.
$\text{Cl-Cl} \rightarrow \text{Cl}^\bullet + \text{Cl}^\bullet$

2. Propagation step: A free radical reacts with a neutral molecule to generate a new free radical and a new neutral molecule. This step keeps the chain reaction going.
$\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-Cl} + \text{Cl}^\bullet$

3. Termination step: Two free radicals combine to form a neutral molecule, stopping the chain reaction.
$\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{Cl}^\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-Cl}$
$\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{CH}_3^\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_3$

Therefore, the reaction $\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-Cl} + \text{Cl}^\bullet$ represents the propagation step.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the pH of 1 molar HCl solution? (assume complete dissociation)
questions.solution:
HCl is a strong acid and dissociates completely in water.

$HCl \rightarrow H^+ + Cl^-$

For a $1\text{ M}$ solution of HCl, the concentration of hydrogen ions is:

$[H^+] = 1\text{ M}$

$\text{pH} = -\log_{10}[H^+]$

$\text{pH} = -\log_{10}(1) = 0$

Answer: Zero

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the pH of buffer solution containing 0.1M $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ and 0.1 M $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}[K_a = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}]$
questions.solution:
Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer:

$\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]} \right)$

Given $[\text{Salt}] = 0.1 \text{ M}$ and $[\text{Acid}] = 0.1 \text{ M}$

$\text{pH} = -\log(1.8 \times 10^{-5}) + \log \left( \dfrac{0.1}{0.1} \right)$

$\text{pH} = 5 - \log(1.8) + \log(1)$

$\text{pH} = 5 - 0.255 + 0 = 4.745$

Answer: $4.745$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: There are two different solutions, A and B. The pH of solution A is 4. Find the pH of solution B having $[\text{H}^+]$ three times that of solution A.
questions.solution:
The pH of solution A is given as $4$.

$[\text{H}^+]_A = 10^{-4} \text{ M}$

For solution B, the hydrogen ion concentration is three times that of solution A.

$[\text{H}^+]_B = 3 \times [\text{H}^+]_A = 3 \times 10^{-4} \text{ M}$

$\text{pH of solution B} = -\log[\text{H}^+]_B$

$\text{pH} = -\log(3 \times 10^{-4})$

$\text{pH} = 4 - \log 3$

Using $\log 3 = 0.4771$:

$\text{pH} = 4 - 0.4771 = 3.5229$

Answer: $3.5229$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In Haber process of production of ammonia $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is used as
questions.solution:
In the Haber process for the synthesis of ammonia, finely divided iron is used as the catalyst.

To enhance the activity of the iron catalyst, small amounts of aluminum oxide ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) and potassium oxide ($\text{K}_2\text{O}$) are added.

Substances that increase the efficiency or activity of a catalyst are known as promoters. Therefore, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ acts as a promoter.

Answer: Promoter

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a cross-linked, thermosetting polymer?
questions.solution:
Bakelite is formed by the condensation reaction of phenol with formaldehyde. It is a highly cross-linked, thermosetting polymer which, once molded, cannot be remolded or reshaped by heating.

PVC, Polystyrene, and PTFE (Teflon) are examples of thermoplastic polymers, which can be repeatedly softened by heating and hardened by cooling.

Answer: Bakelite

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is fully Fluorinated polymer?
questions.solution:
Teflon is the commercial name for polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE).

The monomer of Teflon is tetrafluoroethylene, which has the chemical formula $CF_2=CF_2$.

Since all the hydrogen atoms in the ethylene monomer are replaced by fluorine atoms, Teflon is a fully fluorinated polymer.

PVC (polyvinyl chloride) contains chlorine and hydrogen, neoprene contains chlorine and hydrogen, and Buna-S is a hydrocarbon polymer containing only carbon and hydrogen.

Answer: Teflon

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of electrons gained by Cl atom when $n$ mole of $\text{ClO}_4^-$ is transformed into $n$ mole of $\text{ClO}_2^-$ ion?
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of Cl in $\text{ClO}_4^-$ be $x$.

$x + 4(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x = +7$

Let the oxidation state of Cl in $\text{ClO}_2^-$ be $y$.

$y + 2(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow y = +3$

The change in oxidation state of Cl is from $+7$ to $+3$. This means each Cl atom gains $4$ electrons during the transformation.

For $1$ mole of $\text{ClO}_4^-$, $4$ moles of electrons are gained.

Therefore, for $n$ moles of $\text{ClO}_4^-$, the number of moles of electrons gained is $4n$.

Answer: $4n$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of Cl in $\text{HOClO}_2$?
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation number of $\text{Cl}$ in $\text{HOClO}_2$ (which is $\text{HClO}_3$) be $x$.

The oxidation number of hydrogen ($\text{H}$) is $+1$ and that of oxygen ($\text{O}$) is $-2$.

The sum of the oxidation numbers of all atoms in a neutral molecule is zero.

$+1 + x + 3(-2) = 0$

$x - 5 = 0$

$x = +5$

The oxidation number of $\text{Cl}$ in $\text{HOClO}_2$ is $+5$.

Answer: $+5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of Xe in $\text{XeOF}_4$?
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of Xe in $\text{XeOF}_4$ be $x$.

The oxidation state of oxygen (O) is $-2$ and that of fluorine (F) is $-1$.

Since the molecule is neutral, the sum of the oxidation states of all atoms must be zero.

$x + (-2) + 4(-1) = 0$

$x - 2 - 4 = 0$

$x - 6 = 0$

$x = +6$

The oxidation state of Xe in $\text{XeOF}_4$ is $+6$.

Answer: $+6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose a false statement regarding the properties of sodium hydroxide.
options: the solution of NaOH turns blue litmus red.
NaOH is a white deliquescent solid.
questions.solution:
Sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) is a strong base. Basic solutions turn red litmus paper blue. Therefore, the statement that the solution of $\text{NaOH}$ turns blue litmus red is false.

The other statements are true:
$\text{NaOH}$ is highly soluble in water.
It reacts with atmospheric $\text{CO}_2$ to form sodium carbonate ($\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$).
It is a white, deliquescent solid that readily absorbs moisture from the air.

Answer: the solution of NaOH turns blue litmus red.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following defects is observed in steel?
questions.solution:
Steel is an alloy composed primarily of iron and a small amount of carbon.

In the crystal lattice of iron, the much smaller carbon atoms occupy the interstitial voids between the iron atoms.

When foreign atoms occupy the interstitial sites of a host lattice, the defect is known as an interstitial impurity defect.

Therefore, steel exhibits an interstitial impurity defect.

Answer: Interstitial impurity defect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A metal has a fcc structure if the edge length of unit cell is 200 pm, calculate the volume occupied by particles in a unit cell.
questions.solution:
Edge length of the unit cell, $a = 200 \text{ pm} = 2 \times 10^{-8} \text{ cm}$

Volume of the unit cell, $V = a^3 = (2 \times 10^{-8})^3 = 8 \times 10^{-24} \text{ cm}^3$

For a face-centered cubic (fcc) structure, the packing efficiency is $74\%$.

Volume occupied by particles in the unit cell = $0.74 \times V$

$= 0.74 \times 8 \times 10^{-24} \text{ cm}^3$

$= 5.92 \times 10^{-24} \text{ cm}^3$

Answer: $5.92 \times 10^{-24}\ \text{cm}^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A metal crystallizes in a bcc unit cell having unit cell volume $2.5 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$. Find the number of unit cells in 18 g metal if the density of metal is $7.2\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$.
questions.solution:
Total volume of the metal is given by the ratio of mass to density.

$V_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Density}} = \dfrac{18}{7.2} = 2.5\ \text{cm}^3$

The number of unit cells is the total volume divided by the volume of one unit cell.

$\text{Number of unit cells} = \dfrac{V_{\text{total}}}{V_{\text{unit cell}}} = \dfrac{2.5}{2.5 \times 10^{-23}} = 1.0 \times 10^{23}$

Answer: $1.0 \times 10^{23}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the colligative property from the followings?
questions.solution:
Colligative properties depend only on the number of solute particles in a solution and not on their nature.

The four colligative properties are:
1. Relative lowering of vapour pressure
2. Elevation in boiling point
3. Depression in freezing point
4. Osmotic pressure

Vapour pressure, boiling point, and freezing point of a solution are not colligative properties themselves. Osmotic pressure of a solution is a colligative property.

Answer: Osmotic pressure of solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the osmotic pressure of 0.01 M solution at 25 °C $(R = 0.0821\ \text{L atm mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1})$
questions.solution:
The osmotic pressure $\pi$ is given by the formula:

$\pi = CRT$

Here, $C = 0.01$ M, $T = 25^\circ\text{C} = 298$ K, and $R = 0.0821$ L atm mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$.

$\pi = 0.01 \times 0.0821 \times 298$

$\pi = 0.244658$ atm $\approx 0.245$ atm

Answer: $0.245$ atm

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
When the bottle of soft drink is opened, what would take place from the following?
(A) Solubility of dissolved gas decreases.
(B) bottle released internal pressure.
(C) effervences evolved from the bottle.
(D) increase in external pressure.
Identify the correct choice.
questions.solution:
Soft drinks are bottled under high pressure to increase the solubility of $CO_2$ gas in the liquid, according to Henry's law.

When the bottle is opened, the high internal pressure is released to match the atmospheric pressure. Thus, statement (B) is correct.

As the pressure decreases, the solubility of the dissolved gas decreases. Thus, statement (A) is correct.

The excess dissolved gas escapes rapidly in the form of bubbles, causing effervescence. Thus, statement (C) is correct.

The external atmospheric pressure remains constant and does not increase. Thus, statement (D) is incorrect.

Therefore, only (A), (B), and (C) take place.

Answer: (A), (B) and (C) only.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of molecules in 2.125 g of ammonia?
questions.solution:
Molar mass of ammonia ($NH_3$) = $14 + 3 = 17 \text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles of ammonia = $\dfrac{2.125}{17} = 0.125 \text{ mol}$

Number of molecules = $0.125 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 7.527 \times 10^{22}$

Answer: $7.527 \times 10^{22}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A mixture of 0.5 mol $\text{N}_2$ gas, 1.0 mol $\text{O}_2$ gas and 1.5 mol $\text{H}_2$ gas exerts a total pressure of 18 bar. Find the partial pressure of $\text{O}_{2(g)}$.
questions.solution:
Total number of moles in the mixture is:

$n_{total} = n_{N_2} + n_{O_2} + n_{H_2}$

$n_{total} = 0.5 + 1.0 + 1.5 = 3.0$ mol

Mole fraction of $\text{O}_2$ is:

$x_{O_2} = \dfrac{n_{O_2}}{n_{total}} = \dfrac{1.0}{3.0} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

According to Dalton's law of partial pressures, the partial pressure of $\text{O}_2$ is:

$P_{O_2} = x_{O_2} \times P_{total}$

$P_{O_2} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 18 = 6.0$ bar

Answer: $6.0$ bar

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify pair of orbitals having similar $(n + l)$ values from the following.
questions.solution:
The $(n + l)$ value for an orbital is calculated by adding the principal quantum number $n$ and the azimuthal quantum number $l$.

For $s$, $p$, $d$, and $f$ subshells, the values of $l$ are $0, 1, 2,$ and $3$ respectively.

Calculating $(n + l)$ for the given pairs:

For $3s$ and $3p$: $(3 + 0) = 3$ and $(3 + 1) = 4$

For $2p$ and $4s$: $(2 + 1) = 3$ and $(4 + 0) = 4$

For $3d$ and $4p$: $(3 + 2) = 5$ and $(4 + 1) = 5$

For $2p$ and $3p$: $(2 + 1) = 3$ and $(3 + 1) = 4$

The pair $3d$ and $4p$ has the same $(n + l)$ value of $5$.

Answer: 3d and 4p

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following nanomaterials has one dimension $\lt  100$ nm?
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are classified based on the number of dimensions that lie in the nanoscale range ($1$ to $100$ nm).

Zero-dimensional (0D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include quantum dots and nanoparticles.

One-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials have two dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include nanowires and nanotubes.

Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials have exactly one dimension in the nanoscale. Examples include thin films, graphene, and nanosheets.

Three-dimensional (3D) nanomaterials have no dimensions in the nanoscale but possess nanoscale features.

Since thin films have only one dimension (thickness) less than $100$ nm, they are classified as 2D nanomaterials.

Answer: Thin films

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following processes exhibits the decrease in internal energy of a system?
options: Isothermal expansion of an ideal gas.
Isothrmal compression of an ideal gas.
Adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas.
Adiabatic compression of an ideal gas
questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + w$.

For an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant ($\Delta T = 0$). Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, $\Delta U = 0$ for both isothermal expansion and compression.

For an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange with the surroundings, so $q = 0$. The first law becomes $\Delta U = w$.

During adiabatic expansion, work is done by the gas on the surroundings, meaning $w \lt 0$. Consequently, $\Delta U \lt 0$, which indicates a decrease in the internal energy of the system.

During adiabatic compression, work is done on the gas, meaning $w \gt 0$, leading to an increase in internal energy.

Answer: Adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the change in internal energy if an ideal gas expands from $0.5\ \text{dm}^3$ to $3.5\ \text{dm}^3$ at constant pressure 2 bar by absorbing 1800 J heat energy.
questions.solution:
Given $V_1 = 0.5\ \text{dm}^3$, $V_2 = 3.5\ \text{dm}^3$, $P = 2\ \text{bar}$, and heat absorbed $q = 1800\ \text{J}$.

Work done during expansion at constant pressure is given by $W = -P(V_2 - V_1)$.

$W = -2 \times (3.5 - 0.5) = -6\ \text{bar}\cdot\text{dm}^3$

Since $1\ \text{bar}\cdot\text{dm}^3 = 100\ \text{J}$, we have $W = -600\ \text{J}$.

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + W$.

Substituting the values, $\Delta U = 1800 - 600 = 1200\ \text{J}$.

Answer: $1200$ J.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The enthalpy of combustion of C, $\text{H}_2$, and $\text{CH}_4$ are $-390$, $-285$ and $-890$ kJ/mol. Find the enthalpy of formation of methane.
questions.solution:
The required reaction for the formation of methane is:

$\text{C(s)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_4\text{(g)}$

The enthalpy of formation can be calculated using the enthalpies of combustion of the reactants and products:

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = \Delta H_c(\text{C}) + 2\Delta H_c(\text{H}_2) - \Delta H_c(\text{CH}_4)$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = -390 + 2(-285) - (-890)$

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = -390 - 570 + 890$

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = -960 + 890 = -70 \text{ kJ/mol}$

Answer: $-70$ kJ

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The function $f(x) = x(x + 3)e^{-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)x}$ satisfies all the conditions of Rolle's theorem in $[-3, 0]$, then $c =$
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = (x^2 + 3x)e^{-\dfrac{x}{2}}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$f'(x) = (2x + 3)e^{-\dfrac{x}{2}} + (x^2 + 3x)e^{-\dfrac{x}{2}} \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$f'(x) = e^{-\dfrac{x}{2}} \left( 2x + 3 - \dfrac{x^2 + 3x}{2} \right)$

$f'(x) = e^{-\dfrac{x}{2}} \left( \dfrac{-x^2 + x + 6}{2} \right)$

By Rolle's theorem, there exists $c \in (-3, 0)$ such that $f'(c) = 0$.

$\dfrac{-c^2 + c + 6}{2} = 0$

$c^2 - c - 6 = 0$

$(c - 3)(c + 2) = 0$

$c = 3$ or $c = -2$

Since $c \in (-3, 0)$, we get $c = -2$.

Answer: $-2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The line $x + y = 0$ touches the curve $y^2 = ax^3 + b$ at $(1, -1)$ then values of $a$ and $b$ respectively are ...........
questions.solution:
Since the point $(1, -1)$ lies on the curve $y^2 = ax^3 + b$, substituting $x = 1$ and $y = -1$ gives:

$(-1)^2 = a(1)^3 + b$

$a + b = 1$

Differentiating the equation of the curve with respect to $x$ gives:

$2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3ax^2$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3ax^2}{2y}$

The slope of the tangent at $(1, -1)$ is:

$\left. \dfrac{dy}{dx} \right|_{(1, -1)} = \dfrac{3a(1)^2}{2(-1)} = -\dfrac{3a}{2}$

The given tangent line is $x + y = 0$, which has a slope of $-1$. Equating the slopes gives:

$-\dfrac{3a}{2} = -1$

$a = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Substituting the value of $a$ into $a + b = 1$ gives:

$\dfrac{2}{3} + b = 1$

$b = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{1}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An aeroplane at an altitude of 1 km is flying horizontally at 600 km / hr, passes directly over an observer. Then the rate at which it is approaching the observer when it is 1250 meters away from him is........
questions.solution:
Let the horizontal distance of the aeroplane from the observer be $x$ km and the actual distance be $s$ km.

The altitude of the aeroplane is $h = 1$ km.

From the right-angled triangle formed by the observer, the aeroplane, and the point on the ground directly below the aeroplane, we have:

$s^2 = x^2 + 1^2$

Differentiating with respect to time $t$, we get:

$2s \dfrac{ds}{dt} = 2x \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

$\dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{x}{s} \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

We are given the horizontal velocity $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 600$ km/hr.

When the distance $s = 1250$ m $= 1.25$ km, the horizontal distance $x$ is:

$x = \sqrt{s^2 - 1^2} = \sqrt{1.25^2 - 1} = \sqrt{1.5625 - 1} = \sqrt{0.5625} = 0.75$ km

Substituting the values into the derivative equation:

$\dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{0.75}{1.25} \times 600$

$\dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{3}{5} \times 600 = 360$ km/hr

Answer: $360\ km/hr$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area in square units of the region bounded by the curve $y = \sqrt{16 - x^2}$ and lines $x = 0, x = 4$ above the X-axis is
questions.solution:
The given curve is $y = \sqrt{16 - x^2}$, which represents the upper half of the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 16$ with center $(0,0)$ and radius $4$.

The region bounded by the curve, $x = 0$, $x = 4$, and above the X-axis lies entirely in the first quadrant.

The required area is given by the integral:

$A = \int_{0}^{4} \sqrt{16 - x^2} dx$

Using the standard integral formula $\int \sqrt{a^2 - x^2} dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)$, we get:

$A = \left[ \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16 - x^2} + 8\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right) \right]_{0}^{4}$

$A = \left( 0 + 8\sin^{-1}(1) \right) - \left( 0 + 8\sin^{-1}(0) \right)$

$A = 8 \times \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 4\pi$ sq. units.

Answer: $4\pi$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The statement having truth value 'T' from the following is
options: The product of complex number and its conjugate is purely imaginary.
A square of any real number is non-negative.
questions.solution:
Evaluating statement (1): $\sin(-x) = -\sin(x)$, which means $\sin(x)$ is an odd function. The statement is false.

Evaluating statement (2): A square matrix with a zero determinant is a singular matrix. Therefore, not every square matrix is non-singular. The statement is false.

Evaluating statement (3): Let a complex number be $z = x + iy$, its conjugate is $\bar{z} = x - iy$. The product $z\bar{z} = (x + iy)(x - iy) = x^2 + y^2$, which is a purely real number. The statement is false.

Evaluating statement (4): For any real number $x$, the square is $x^2 \ge 0$. The square of any real number is non-negative. The statement is true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of a circle whose center lies on $x + 2y = 0$ and touching the lines $3x - 4y + 8 = 0$ and $3x - 4y - 28 = 0$ is
questions.solution:
The given lines $3x - 4y + 8 = 0$ and $3x - 4y - 28 = 0$ are parallel. The distance between them is the diameter of the circle.

Diameter $= \dfrac{|8 - (-28)|}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-4)^2}} = \dfrac{36}{5}$

Radius $r = \dfrac{18}{5}$

The center of the circle lies on the line parallel to and midway between the two given lines. The equation of this midway line is:

$3x - 4y + \dfrac{8 + (-28)}{2} = 0 \Rightarrow 3x - 4y - 10 = 0$

The center also lies on the given line $x + 2y = 0$.

Solving $3x - 4y - 10 = 0$ and $x + 2y = 0$, we substitute $x = -2y$:

$3(-2y) - 4y - 10 = 0 \Rightarrow -10y = 10 \Rightarrow y = -1$

Substituting $y = -1$ in $x = -2y$, we get $x = 2$.

The center of the circle is $(2, -1)$.

The equation of the circle is:

$(x - 2)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = \left(\dfrac{18}{5}\right)^2$

$(x - 2)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = \dfrac{324}{25}$

$25(x - 2)^2 + 25(y + 1)^2 = 324$

Answer: $25(x - 2)^2 + 25(y + 1)^2 = 324$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $i = \sqrt{-1}$ then $\left[i^{18} + \left(\dfrac{1}{i}\right)^{25}\right]^3 =$
questions.solution:
We know that $i^4 = 1$ and $i^2 = -1$.

Evaluating the first term:

$i^{18} = (i^4)^4 \cdot i^2 = 1 \cdot (-1) = -1$

Evaluating the second term:

$\left(\dfrac{1}{i}\right)^{25} = \dfrac{1}{i^{25}} = \dfrac{1}{(i^4)^6 \cdot i} = \dfrac{1}{i} = -i$

Substituting these values into the given expression:

$\left[i^{18} + \left(\dfrac{1}{i}\right)^{25}\right]^3 = (-1 - i)^3$

$= -(1 + i)^3$

$= -(1^3 + 3(1)^2(i) + 3(1)(i)^2 + i^3)$

$= -(1 + 3i - 3 - i)$

$= -(-2 + 2i)$

$= 2 - 2i$

Answer: $2 - 2i$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the function $f(x)$ defined by $f(x) = \begin{cases} ax + 1 & \text{if } x \leq 3 \\ bx + 3 & \text{if } x  \gt  3 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 3$, then $(a - b) =$ ..........
questions.solution:
For the function $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x = 3$, the left-hand limit must be equal to the right-hand limit and the value of the function at $x = 3$.

$\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = f(3)$

Evaluating the left-hand limit:

$\lim_{x \to 3^-} (ax + 1) = 3a + 1$

Evaluating the right-hand limit:

$\lim_{x \to 3^+} (bx + 3) = 3b + 3$

Equating the limits:

$3a + 1 = 3b + 3$

$3a - 3b = 2$

$3(a - b) = 2$

$a - b = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $I_n = \int\limits_0^{\pi/4}\tan^n x\ dx, n \in N$ then $I_{n+2} + I_n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$I_{n+2} + I_n = \int\limits_0^{\pi/4} \tan^{n+2} x\ dx + \int\limits_0^{\pi/4} \tan^n x\ dx$

$I_{n+2} + I_n = \int\limits_0^{\pi/4} \tan^n x (\tan^2 x + 1)\ dx$

$I_{n+2} + I_n = \int\limits_0^{\pi/4} \tan^n x \sec^2 x\ dx$

Substituting $t = \tan x$, we get $dt = \sec^2 x\ dx$.

When $x = 0$, $t = 0$ and when $x = \pi/4$, $t = 1$.

$I_{n+2} + I_n = \int\limits_0^1 t^n\ dt$

$I_{n+2} + I_n = \left[ \dfrac{t^{n+1}}{n+1} \right]_0^1$

$I_{n+2} + I_n = \dfrac{1}{n+1}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{n + 1}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int\limits_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}(\sin^2 x + \sin^3 x)dx = k$, then the value of $k$
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} (\sin^2 x + \sin^3 x) dx$

$I = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x dx + \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \sin^3 x dx$

Since $\sin^3 x$ is an odd function, $\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \sin^3 x dx = 0$

Since $\sin^2 x$ is an even function, $\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x dx = 2 \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x dx$

$I = 2 \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x dx = 2 \left( \dfrac{\pi}{4} \right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Therefore, $k = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of the integral $\int\limits_{1/e}^{e}\dfrac{|\log x|}{x^2}dx$ is
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int\limits_{1/e}^{e}\dfrac{|\log x|}{x^2}dx$

Substitute $x = e^t \Rightarrow dx = e^t dt$

When $x = 1/e$, $t = -1$ and when $x = e$, $t = 1$

$I = \int\limits_{-1}^{1} \dfrac{|t|}{e^{2t}} e^t dt = \int\limits_{-1}^{1} |t| e^{-t} dt$

Splitting the integral at $t = 0$:

$I = \int\limits_{-1}^{0} -t e^{-t} dt + \int\limits_{0}^{1} t e^{-t} dt$

Using integration by parts:

$\int -t e^{-t} dt = t e^{-t} + e^{-t}$

$\int t e^{-t} dt = -t e^{-t} - e^{-t}$

Evaluating the definite integrals:

$I = \left[ t e^{-t} + e^{-t} \right]_{-1}^{0} + \left[ -t e^{-t} - e^{-t} \right]_{0}^{1}$

$I = \left( (0 + e^0) - (-e^1 + e^1) \right) + \left( (-e^{-1} - e^{-1}) - (0 - e^0) \right)$

$I = (1 - 0) + \left( -\dfrac{2}{e} - (-1) \right)$

$I = 1 + 1 - \dfrac{2}{e} = 2 - \dfrac{2}{e}$

Answer: $2 - \dfrac{2}{e}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $pC_{11} + 4C_{21} - 5C_{32} = -2$, where $C_{ij}$ denotes the cofactor of an element $a_{ij}$ of matrix $A$, then the value of $p$ is :
questions.solution:
Given matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$

The cofactor $C_{ij}$ is given by $(-1)^{i+j} M_{ij}$, where $M_{ij}$ is the minor of the element $a_{ij}$.

Calculating the required cofactors:

$C_{11} = (-1)^{1+1} \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = 1 \times (8 - 0) = 8$

$C_{21} = (-1)^{2+1} \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = -1 \times (4 - 2) = -2$

$C_{32} = (-1)^{3+2} \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = -1 \times (0 - 2) = 2$

Substituting these values into the given equation $pC_{11} + 4C_{21} - 5C_{32} = -2$:

$p(8) + 4(-2) - 5(2) = -2$

$8p - 8 - 10 = -2$

$8p - 18 = -2$

$8p = 16$

$p = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The order and degree of the differential equation $\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}$, respectively are
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

Squaring both sides to remove the fractional powers, we get:

$1 + \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^3$

Multiplying the entire equation by $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$ to express it as a polynomial in derivatives:

$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 1 = \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^3$

The highest order derivative present in the equation is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$, which means the order of the differential equation is $2$.

The power of the highest order derivative in this polynomial form is $3$, which means the degree of the differential equation is $3$.

Therefore, the order and degree are $2$ and $3$, respectively.

Answer: $2, 3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = x^2 + 5$ is ....
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{1}{x}y = x^2 + 5$.

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$, where $P = \dfrac{1}{x}$ and $Q = x^2 + 5$.

The integrating factor is $e^{\int P dx} = e^{\int \dfrac{1}{x} dx} = e^{\ln x} = x$.

Multiplying the equation by the integrating factor, the solution is given by:

$y \cdot x = \int x(x^2 + 5) dx + C$

$xy = \int (x^3 + 5x) dx + C$

$xy = \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{5x^2}{2} + C$

Rearranging the terms, we get:

$\dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{5x^2}{2} - xy = -C$

Taking $-C = c$, the general solution is:

$\dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{5x^2}{2} - xy = c$

Answer: $\dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{5x^2}{2} - xy = c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x = a\sin^3 t$ and $y = a\cos^3 t$, then the value of $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given $x = a\sin^3 t$ and $y = a\cos^3 t$.

Differentiating with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 3a\sin^2 t \cos t$

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -3a\cos^2 t \sin t$

Now, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{dt}}{\dfrac{dx}{dt}} = \dfrac{-3a\cos^2 t \sin t}{3a\sin^2 t \cos t} = -\cot t$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(-\cot t) \cdot \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \csc^2 t \cdot \dfrac{1}{3a\sin^2 t \cos t} = \dfrac{1}{3a\sin^4 t \cos t}$

Substituting $t = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$:

$\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{1}{3a \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^4 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{3a \left(\dfrac{9}{16}\right) \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{32}{27a}$

Answer: $\dfrac{32}{27a}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x = 4t^3 + 3, y = 3t^4 + 4$ and $\dfrac{\frac{d^2x}{dy^2}}{\left(\frac{dx}{dy}\right)^n}$ is constant then the value of $n$ is
questions.solution:
Given $x = 4t^3 + 3$ and $y = 3t^4 + 4$.

Differentiating with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 12t^2$

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 12t^3$

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dx}{dt}}{\dfrac{dy}{dt}} = \dfrac{12t^2}{12t^3} = \dfrac{1}{t} = t^{-1}$

Now, finding the second derivative $\dfrac{d^2x}{dy^2}$:

$\dfrac{d^2x}{dy^2} = \dfrac{d}{dy}\left(\dfrac{dx}{dy}\right) = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(t^{-1}\right) \cdot \dfrac{dt}{dy}$

$\dfrac{d^2x}{dy^2} = -t^{-2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{12t^3} = -\dfrac{1}{12}t^{-5}$

Substituting these into the given expression:

$\dfrac{\dfrac{d^2x}{dy^2}}{\left(\dfrac{dx}{dy}\right)^n} = \dfrac{-\dfrac{1}{12}t^{-5}}{(t^{-1})^n} = -\dfrac{1}{12}t^{n-5}$

For this expression to be a constant, it must be independent of $t$. Therefore, the exponent of $t$ must be zero:

$n - 5 = 0 \Rightarrow n = 5$

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{y}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{y}{x}} = 6$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$
questions.solution:
Given $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{y}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{y}{x}} = 6$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$\dfrac{x}{y} + \dfrac{y}{x} + 2 = 36$

$\dfrac{x}{y} + \dfrac{y}{x} = 34$

$x^2 + y^2 = 34xy$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$2x + 2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 34 \left( y + x \dfrac{dy}{dx} \right)$

Dividing by $2$:

$x + y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 17y + 17x \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:

$x - 17y = (17x - y) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x - 17y}{17x - y}$

Answer: $\dfrac{x - 17y}{17x - y}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y = \cos^2\left[\cot^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}}\right)\right]$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = $ ........
questions.solution:
Let $x = \cos \theta$.

Substituting this in the given expression:

$\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos \theta}{1 + \cos \theta}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \sin^2(\theta/2)}{2 \cos^2(\theta/2)}} = \tan\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

The expression for $y$ becomes:

$y = \cos^2\left[\cot^{-1}\left(\tan\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right)\right]$

Using the identity $\tan\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) = \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$:

$y = \cos^2\left[\cot^{-1}\left(\cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right)\right]$

$y = \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

$y = \sin^2\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

Using the half-angle formula $\sin^2\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1 - \cos \theta}{2}$:

$y = \dfrac{1 - x}{2}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{x}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{-1}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x), g(x)$ be twice differentiable functions, satisfying $f''(x) = g''(x), f'(1) = 2g'(1) = 4$ and $f(2) = 3g(2) = 9$ then $f(x) - g(x)$ at $x = 4$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $h(x) = f(x) - g(x)$.

Given $f''(x) = g''(x)$, we have $h''(x) = 0$.

Integrating with respect to $x$, we get $h'(x) = c_1$.

We are given $f'(1) = 4$ and $2g'(1) = 4 \Rightarrow g'(1) = 2$.

Thus, $h'(1) = f'(1) - g'(1) = 4 - 2 = 2$.

Since $h'(x)$ is constant, $h'(x) = 2$.

Integrating again with respect to $x$, we get $h(x) = 2x + c_2$.

We are given $f(2) = 9$ and $3g(2) = 9 \Rightarrow g(2) = 3$.

Thus, $h(2) = f(2) - g(2) = 9 - 3 = 6$.

Substituting $x = 2$ into $h(x) = 2x + c_2$, we get $4 + c_2 = 6 \Rightarrow c_2 = 2$.

Therefore, $h(x) = 2x + 2$.

At $x = 4$, $h(4) = 2(4) + 2 = 10$.

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $P$ be any point on the ellipse $16x^2 + 25y^2 = 400$ with foci $S$ and $S'$ and area of $\triangle PSS'$ is 9 square units, then the abscissa of point $P$ is...........
questions.solution:
The equation of the ellipse is $16x^2 + 25y^2 = 400$, which can be written as $\dfrac{x^2}{25} + \dfrac{y^2}{16} = 1$.

Here, $a^2 = 25$ and $b^2 = 16$.

The eccentricity $e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{b^2}{a^2}} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{16}{25}} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

The foci $S$ and $S'$ are at $(\pm ae, 0) = (\pm 3, 0)$.

The distance between the foci is $SS' = 6$.

Let the coordinates of point $P$ be $(x, y)$. The area of $\triangle PSS'$ is given by $\dfrac{1}{2} \times SS' \times |y|$.

Given that the area is $9$ square units, we have:

$\dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times |y| = 9 \Rightarrow 3|y| = 9 \Rightarrow |y| = 3$

Substituting $y^2 = 9$ into the equation of the ellipse:

$16x^2 + 25(9) = 400$

$16x^2 + 225 = 400$

$16x^2 = 175$

$x^2 = \dfrac{175}{16}$

$x = \pm \dfrac{5\sqrt{7}}{4}$

The abscissa of point $P$ is $\pm \dfrac{5\sqrt{7}}{4}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{5\sqrt{7}}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x) = \dfrac{2x - 1}{x + 5}$, $x \neq -5$ then $f^{-1}(x)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $y = \dfrac{2x - 1}{x + 5}$

$y(x + 5) = 2x - 1$

$xy + 5y = 2x - 1$

$x(y - 2) = -5y - 1$

$x = \dfrac{5y + 1}{2 - y}$

Therefore, $f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{5x + 1}{2 - x}$, $x \neq 2$

Answer: $\dfrac{5x + 1}{2 - x}$, $x \neq 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the given integral be $I = \int (x^{21} + x^6 + x^3)(2x^{18} + 7x^3 + 14)^{\dfrac{1}{3}}\ dx$.

Factoring out $x$ from the first polynomial, we get:

$I = \int x(x^{20} + x^5 + x^2)(2x^{18} + 7x^3 + 14)^{\dfrac{1}{3}}\ dx$

Moving $x$ inside the cube root as $x^3$, we obtain:

$I = \int (x^{20} + x^5 + x^2)(2x^{21} + 7x^6 + 14x^3)^{\dfrac{1}{3}}\ dx$

Let $2x^{21} + 7x^6 + 14x^3 = t$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$(42x^{20} + 42x^5 + 42x^2)\ dx = dt$

$42(x^{20} + x^5 + x^2)\ dx = dt$

$(x^{20} + x^5 + x^2)\ dx = \dfrac{dt}{42}$

Substituting this into the integral, we get:

$I = \int t^{\dfrac{1}{3}} \dfrac{dt}{42}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{42} \dfrac{t^{\dfrac{4}{3}}}{\dfrac{4}{3}} + c$

$I = \dfrac{1}{56} t^{\dfrac{4}{3}} + c$

Substituting back $t = 2x^{21} + 7x^6 + 14x^3$:

$I = \dfrac{1}{56} (2x^{21} + 7x^6 + 14x^3)^{\dfrac{4}{3}} + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2x - x^2}}dx =$
questions.solution:
The given integral is $I = \int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2x - x^2}}dx$

Completing the square for the expression inside the square root:

$2x - x^2 = -(x^2 - 2x) = 1 - (x^2 - 2x + 1) = 1 - (x - 1)^2$

Substituting this into the integral:

$I = \int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - (x - 1)^2}}dx$

Using the standard integration formula $\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}}dx = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right) + c$:

$I = \sin^{-1}(x - 1) + c$

Answer: $\sin^{-1}(x - 1) + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int\dfrac{\log x}{(1 + \log x)^2}dx =$
questions.solution:
Let $\log x = t \Rightarrow x = e^t \Rightarrow dx = e^t dt$

Substituting in the integral:

$I = \int \dfrac{t}{(1 + t)^2} e^t dt$

$I = \int e^t \left( \dfrac{t + 1 - 1}{(1 + t)^2} \right) dt$

$I = \int e^t \left( \dfrac{1}{1 + t} - \dfrac{1}{(1 + t)^2} \right) dt$

This is of the form $\int e^t (f(t) + f'(t)) dt = e^t f(t) + c$, where $f(t) = \dfrac{1}{1 + t}$.

$I = \dfrac{e^t}{1 + t} + c$

Substituting $t = \log x$ and $e^t = x$:

$I = \dfrac{x}{1 + \log x} + c$

Answer: $\dfrac{x}{1 + \log x} + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int f(x)dx = g(x) + c$ then $\int f^{-1}(x)dx =$
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int f^{-1}(x) dx$

Substitute $f^{-1}(x) = t \Rightarrow x = f(t) \Rightarrow dx = f'(t) dt$

$I = \int t f'(t) dt$

Applying integration by parts, taking $t$ as the first function and $f'(t)$ as the second function:

$I = t \int f'(t) dt - \int \left( \dfrac{d}{dt}(t) \int f'(t) dt \right) dt$

$I = t f(t) - \int f(t) dt$

Given $\int f(x) dx = g(x) + c$, we have $\int f(t) dt = g(t) + c$

$I = t f(t) - g(t) + C$

Substituting $t = f^{-1}(x)$ and $f(t) = x$:

$I = x f^{-1}(x) - g(f^{-1}(x)) + C$

Answer: $xf^{-1}(x) - g(f^{-1}(x)) + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $E = 2\sin^{-1}x + 3\cos^{-1}x$

Given $2\sin^{-1}x - 3\cos^{-1}x = 4$

Adding the two equations, we get:

$4\sin^{-1}x = E + 4 \Rightarrow \sin^{-1}x = \dfrac{E + 4}{4}$

Subtracting the second equation from the first, we get:

$6\cos^{-1}x = E - 4 \Rightarrow \cos^{-1}x = \dfrac{E - 4}{6}$

Using the identity $\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:

$\dfrac{E + 4}{4} + \dfrac{E - 4}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$\dfrac{3(E + 4) + 2(E - 4)}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$\dfrac{5E + 4}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$5E + 4 = 6\pi$

$E = \dfrac{6\pi - 4}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{6\pi - 4}{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 + x^2}\right) - 4\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^2}{1 + x^2}\right) + 2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 - x^2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ then $x = ?$
questions.solution:
Assuming $0 \lt x \lt 1$, the standard inverse trigonometric identities are:

$\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 + x^2}\right) = 2\tan^{-1}x$

$\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^2}{1 + x^2}\right) = 2\tan^{-1}x$

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 - x^2}\right) = 2\tan^{-1}x$

Substituting these into the given equation yields:

$3(2\tan^{-1}x) - 4(2\tan^{-1}x) + 2(2\tan^{-1}x) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$6\tan^{-1}x - 8\tan^{-1}x + 4\tan^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$2\tan^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$\tan^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$x = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

Since $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ satisfies the condition $0 \lt x \lt 1$, it is the valid solution.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{1}{1 - n^2} + \dfrac{2}{1 - n^2} + \ldots + \dfrac{n}{1 - n^2}\right]^3$ is
questions.solution:
Let $L = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{1}{1 - n^2} + \dfrac{2}{1 - n^2} + \ldots + \dfrac{n}{1 - n^2}\right]^3$

The expression inside the bracket can be simplified by taking the common denominator:

$S_n = \dfrac{1 + 2 + \ldots + n}{1 - n^2}$

Using the sum of the first $n$ natural numbers, $1 + 2 + \ldots + n = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$:

$S_n = \dfrac{\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}}{1 - n^2}$

$S_n = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2(1 - n)(1 + n)}$

$S_n = \dfrac{n}{2(1 - n)}$

Taking the limit as $n \to \infty$:

$\lim\limits_{n \to \infty} S_n = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \dfrac{n}{2(1 - n)} = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \dfrac{1}{2\left(\dfrac{1}{n} - 1\right)} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore, the required limit is:

$L = \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 = -\dfrac{1}{8}$

Answer: $\dfrac{-1}{8}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The LPP maximize $z = 2x + 5y$ subject to $x + 3y \leq 6$, $2x + 6y \leq 18$, $x \geq 0$, $y \geq 0$ has
questions.solution:
The given constraints are:
$x + 3y \leq 6$
$2x + 6y \leq 18 \Rightarrow x + 3y \leq 9$
$x \geq 0, y \geq 0$

The second constraint $x + 3y \leq 9$ is redundant since $x + 3y \leq 6$ is a stricter condition. The feasible region is bounded by $x + 3y \leq 6$ in the first quadrant, which forms a triangle.

The vertices of the feasible region are $(0,0)$, $(6,0)$, and $(0,2)$.

Evaluating the objective function $z = 2x + 5y$ at these vertices:
At $(0,0)$, $z = 2(0) + 5(0) = 0$
At $(6,0)$, $z = 2(6) + 5(0) = 12$
At $(0,2)$, $z = 2(0) + 5(2) = 10$

The maximum value of $z$ is $12$, which occurs exactly at one vertex $(6,0)$.

Therefore, the LPP has a unique solution.

Answer: Unique solution

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The contrapositive of $\sim q \rightarrow p$ is equivalent to
questions.solution:
The contrapositive of a conditional statement $A \rightarrow B$ is $\sim B \rightarrow \sim A$.

For the given statement $\sim q \rightarrow p$, the contrapositive is $\sim p \rightarrow \sim (\sim q)$.

This simplifies to $\sim p \rightarrow q$.

Using the logical equivalence $X \rightarrow Y \equiv \sim X \vee Y$, we get:

$\sim p \rightarrow q \equiv \sim (\sim p) \vee q \equiv p \vee q$.

Answer: $p \vee q$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sim p \vee q$ is false then which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
Given $\sim p \vee q$ is false.

A disjunction is false only when both of its components are false.

Therefore, $\sim p$ is false and $q$ is false.

This implies $p$ is true ($T$) and $q$ is false ($F$).

Checking the given options:

$p \leftrightarrow q \equiv T \leftrightarrow F \equiv F$

$p \rightarrow q \equiv T \rightarrow F \equiv F$

$q \rightarrow p \equiv F \rightarrow T \equiv T$

Thus, $q \rightarrow p$ is $T$.

Answer: $q \rightarrow p$ is $T$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -5 \\ -2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$, then $A^{-1} =$
questions.solution:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -5 \\ -2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$

The determinant of $A$ is $|A| = (1)(4) - (-5)(-2) = 4 - 10 = -6$

The adjoint of $A$ is obtained by interchanging the diagonal elements and changing the signs of the off-diagonal elements:

$\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

The inverse of the matrix is given by $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|} \text{adj}(A)$

$A^{-1} = -\dfrac{1}{6} \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the angle made by the lines represented by the equation $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$ with X-axis are $\alpha$ and $\beta$, then $\tan(\alpha + \beta)$ is
questions.solution:
Let the slopes of the lines represented by $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$ be $m_1$ and $m_2$.

Since the lines make angles $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with the X-axis, we have $m_1 = \tan \alpha$ and $m_2 = \tan \beta$.

From the given homogeneous equation, dividing by $x^2$ gives $b\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2 + 2h\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + a = 0$.

The roots of this quadratic equation in $m = \dfrac{y}{x}$ are $m_1$ and $m_2$.

Sum of the roots: $m_1 + m_2 = \tan \alpha + \tan \beta = -\dfrac{2h}{b}$

Product of the roots: $m_1 m_2 = \tan \alpha \tan \beta = \dfrac{a}{b}$

Using the trigonometric identity for the tangent of a sum:

$\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{\tan \alpha + \tan \beta}{1 - \tan \alpha \tan \beta}$

Substituting the values of the sum and product of the slopes:

$\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{-\dfrac{2h}{b}}{1 - \dfrac{a}{b}}$

$\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{-\dfrac{2h}{b}}{\dfrac{b - a}{b}}$

$\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{-2h}{b - a} = \dfrac{2h}{a - b}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2h}{a - b}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The number of permutations of the letters of the word INSTITUTION are .......
questions.solution:
The word INSTITUTION has $11$ letters.

The frequencies of the letters are:
I appears $3$ times.
N appears $2$ times.
T appears $3$ times.
S, U, O appear $1$ time each.

The total number of permutations is given by $\dfrac{11!}{3! \times 2! \times 3!}$.

$\dfrac{11!}{3! \times 2! \times 3!} = \dfrac{39916800}{6 \times 2 \times 6} = \dfrac{39916800}{72} = 554400$

Answer: $554400$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A fair die is rolled indefinitely. Player A wins if two consecutive rolls show 3 or 5, and player B wins if two consecutive rolls show 1 or 2 or 4 or 6. The probability that player A wins in the long run is
questions.solution:
Let $S$ be the event of rolling a $3$ or $5$. The probability of this event is $P(S) = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Let $F$ be the event of rolling a $1, 2, 4,$ or $6$. The probability of this event is $P(F) = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Let $P$ be the probability that player A wins the game.
Let $P_S$ be the probability that player A wins given that the previous roll was $S$.
Let $P_F$ be the probability that player A wins given that the previous roll was $F$.

From the start of the game, the first roll is either $S$ or $F$:
$P = \dfrac{1}{3} P_S + \dfrac{2}{3} P_F$

If the previous roll was $S$, rolling another $S$ means A wins immediately. Rolling an $F$ transitions the state to $F$:
$P_S = \dfrac{1}{3}(1) + \dfrac{2}{3} P_F$

If the previous roll was $F$, rolling another $F$ means B wins immediately (so A's chance of winning becomes $0$). Rolling an $S$ transitions the state to $S$:
$P_F = \dfrac{1}{3} P_S + \dfrac{2}{3}(0) = \dfrac{1}{3} P_S$

Substituting $P_F$ into the equation for $P_S$:
$P_S = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3} \left( \dfrac{1}{3} P_S \right)$

$P_S = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{2}{9} P_S$

$\left( 1 - \dfrac{2}{9} \right) P_S = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$\dfrac{7}{9} P_S = \dfrac{1}{3} \Rightarrow P_S = \dfrac{3}{7}$

Now, find $P_F$:
$P_F = \dfrac{1}{3} \left( \dfrac{3}{7} \right) = \dfrac{1}{7}$

Finally, substitute $P_S$ and $P_F$ back into the equation for $P$:
$P = \dfrac{1}{3} \left( \dfrac{3}{7} \right) + \dfrac{2}{3} \left( \dfrac{1}{7} \right)$

$P = \dfrac{1}{7} + \dfrac{2}{21} = \dfrac{3}{21} + \dfrac{2}{21} = \dfrac{5}{21}$

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{21}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following probability distribution of a random variable $X$, the Expected value and Variance of $X$ are respectively
$X = x$$1$$2$$3$
$P(X = x)$$1/5$$2/5$$2/5$
questions.solution:
The expected value of $X$ is given by $E(X) = \sum x_i P(x_i)$

$E(X) = 1 \times \dfrac{1}{5} + 2 \times \dfrac{2}{5} + 3 \times \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{4}{5} + \dfrac{6}{5} = \dfrac{11}{5}$

The expected value of $X^2$ is given by $E(X^2) = \sum x_i^2 P(x_i)$

$E(X^2) = 1^2 \times \dfrac{1}{5} + 2^2 \times \dfrac{2}{5} + 3^2 \times \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{8}{5} + \dfrac{18}{5} = \dfrac{27}{5}$

The variance of $X$ is given by $Var(X) = E(X^2) - (E(X))^2$

$Var(X) = \dfrac{27}{5} - \left(\dfrac{11}{5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{27}{5} - \dfrac{121}{25} = \dfrac{135 - 121}{25} = \dfrac{14}{25}$

Answer: $\dfrac{11}{5}, \dfrac{14}{25}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Four cards are drawn successively with replacement from well shuffled deck of 52 cards, then the probability that only two cards are club cards is ...........
questions.solution:
Probability of drawing a club card, $p = \dfrac{13}{52} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Probability of not drawing a club card, $q = 1 - p = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Number of trials, $n = 4$

Number of successes, $r = 2$

Using binomial distribution, $P(X = r) = ^{n}C_{r} p^{r} q^{n-r}$

$P(X = 2) = ^{4}C_{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{2} \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{2}$

$P(X = 2) = 6 \times \dfrac{1}{16} \times \dfrac{9}{16}$

$P(X = 2) = \dfrac{54}{256} = \dfrac{27}{128}$

Answer: $\dfrac{27}{128}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: With the usual notations, if the lengths of the sides of the triangle are 3 units, 5 units and 7 units, then the largest angle of the triangle is
questions.solution:
Let the sides of the triangle be $a = 3$, $b = 5$, and $c = 7$.

The largest angle of a triangle is opposite to its longest side. Thus, the largest angle is $C$, which is opposite to the side $c = 7$.

Using the cosine rule:

$\cos C = \dfrac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab}$

Substituting the given values:

$\cos C = \dfrac{3^2 + 5^2 - 7^2}{2(3)(5)}$

$\cos C = \dfrac{9 + 25 - 49}{30}$

$\cos C = \dfrac{34 - 49}{30}$

$\cos C = \dfrac{-15}{30} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $0 \lt C \lt \pi$, we get $C = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angles of $\triangle ABC$ are in A.P. and $b : c = \sqrt{3} : \sqrt{2}$ then $\angle A =$
questions.solution:
Given angles $A, B, C$ are in A.P.

$2B = A + C$

Since $A + B + C = 180^\circ$, we have $3B = 180^\circ \Rightarrow B = 60^\circ$

Using the sine rule, $\dfrac{b}{\sin B} = \dfrac{c}{\sin C}$

Substituting the given ratio $\dfrac{b}{c} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $B = 60^\circ$:

$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sin 60^\circ}{\sin C}$

$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{\sin C}$

$\sin C = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Since $B = 60^\circ$, $C$ cannot be $135^\circ$ (as $B + C = 195^\circ \gt 180^\circ$), so $C = 45^\circ$

The sum of angles in a triangle is $180^\circ$:

$A + B + C = 180^\circ$

$A + 60^\circ + 45^\circ = 180^\circ$

$A = 75^\circ$

Answer: $75^\circ$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A straight line makes equal negative intercepts on the coordinate axes. If the perpendicular distance from the origin to the line is 4 units, then the equation of the line is ......
questions.solution:
Let the equation of the line in intercept form be $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1$.

Since the line makes equal negative intercepts on the coordinate axes, $a = b = -c$ where $c \gt 0$.

The equation of the line becomes $\dfrac{x}{-c} + \dfrac{y}{-c} = 1 \Rightarrow x + y + c = 0$.

The perpendicular distance from the origin $(0,0)$ to this line is given as $4$ units.

Using the perpendicular distance formula, $\dfrac{|0 + 0 + c|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}} = 4$.

$\dfrac{|c|}{\sqrt{2}} = 4 \Rightarrow |c| = 4\sqrt{2}$.

Since $c \gt 0$, we have $c = 4\sqrt{2}$.

Substituting the value of $c$ in the equation of the line, we get $x + y + 4\sqrt{2} = 0$.

Answer: $x + y + 4\sqrt{2} = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The Cartesian equations of the line passing through $A(0, 1, 1)$ and parallel to the X-axis are ....
questions.solution:
The direction ratios of the X-axis are $1, 0, 0$.

The line passes through the point $A(0, 1, 1)$ and is parallel to the X-axis. Therefore, its direction ratios are $1, 0, 0$.

The Cartesian equations of the line are given by:

$\dfrac{x - 0}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{0} = \dfrac{z - 1}{0}$

This implies $y - 1 = 0$ and $z - 1 = 0$.

Thus, the equations of the line are $y = 1, z = 1$.

Answer: $y = 1, z = 1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Lines $\vec{r} = \vec{a} + \lambda\vec{b}$ and $\vec{r} = \vec{b} + \mu\vec{a}$ intersect at point $(2, 4, -4)$. If $|\vec{a} - \vec{b}| = 4$, then $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} =$
questions.solution:
Let the point of intersection be $\vec{p} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$.

Since the lines intersect at $\vec{p}$, there exist scalars $\lambda$ and $\mu$ such that:

$\vec{a} + \lambda\vec{b} = \vec{b} + \mu\vec{a}$

$\Rightarrow (1 - \mu)\vec{a} + (\lambda - 1)\vec{b} = \vec{0}$

Assuming $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are non-collinear, we get $1 - \mu = 0$ and $\lambda - 1 = 0$, which gives $\lambda = 1$ and $\mu = 1$.

Thus, the position vector of the point of intersection is:

$\vec{p} = \vec{a} + \vec{b}$

The magnitude squared of $\vec{p}$ is:

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b}|^2 = 2^2 + 4^2 + (-4)^2 = 4 + 16 + 16 = 36$

We are given $|\vec{a} - \vec{b}| = 4$, so:

$|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^2 = 16$

Using the vector identity:

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b}|^2 - |\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^2 = 4\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}$

Substituting the values:

$36 - 16 = 4\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}$

$20 = 4\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}$

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 5$

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the line joining points $(2, 1, 4)$ and $(a - 1, 4, -1)$ is parallel to the line joining points $(0, 2, b - 1)$ and $(5, 3, -2)$ then the values of $b$ and $a$ are respectively
questions.solution:
Direction ratios of the line joining $(2, 1, 4)$ and $(a - 1, 4, -1)$ are $(a - 1 - 2, 4 - 1, -1 - 4) = (a - 3, 3, -5)$.

Direction ratios of the line joining $(0, 2, b - 1)$ and $(5, 3, -2)$ are $(5 - 0, 3 - 2, -2 - (b - 1)) = (5, 1, -b - 1)$.

Since the lines are parallel, their direction ratios are proportional:

$\dfrac{a - 3}{5} = \dfrac{3}{1} = \dfrac{-5}{-b - 1}$

From $\dfrac{a - 3}{5} = 3$, we get $a - 3 = 15 \Rightarrow a = 18$.

From $\dfrac{-5}{-b - 1} = 3$, we get $-5 = -3b - 3 \Rightarrow 3b = 2 \Rightarrow b = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

The values of $b$ and $a$ respectively are $\dfrac{2}{3}, 18$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}, 18$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the perpendicular distance of the plane passing through the point $Q(1, 0, -1)$ and containing the line $\vec{r} = (\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}) + \lambda(2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k})$ from origin is $\dfrac{p}{\sqrt{53}}$ then $p = $ ...
questions.solution:
The plane contains the point $Q(1, 0, -1)$ and the line $\vec{r} = (\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}) + \lambda(2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k})$.

The line passes through the point $A(1, -3, 1)$ and has the direction vector $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

Since the plane contains both the point $Q$ and the line, it contains the vector $\overrightarrow{QA}$ joining $Q$ and $A$.

$\overrightarrow{QA} = (1 - 1)\hat{i} + (-3 - 0)\hat{j} + (1 - (-1))\hat{k} = -3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

The normal vector $\vec{n}$ to the plane is perpendicular to both $\vec{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{QA}$.

$\vec{n} = \vec{b} \times \overrightarrow{QA} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{n} = \hat{i}(-4 - (-3)) - \hat{j}(4 - 0) + \hat{k}(-6 - 0) = -\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} - 6\hat{k}$

Taking the normal vector as $\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$, the equation of the plane passing through $Q(1, 0, -1)$ is:

$1(x - 1) + 4(y - 0) + 6(z + 1) = 0$

$x + 4y + 6z + 5 = 0$

The perpendicular distance of this plane from the origin $(0, 0, 0)$ is:

$d = \dfrac{|1(0) + 4(0) + 6(0) + 5|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 4^2 + 6^2}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{1 + 16 + 36}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{53}}$

Comparing this with the given distance $\dfrac{p}{\sqrt{53}}$, we get $p = 5$.

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x + y = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, then $(1 + \tan x)(1 + \tan y) =$
questions.solution:
Given $x + y = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Taking $\tan$ on both sides:

$\tan(x + y) = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

$\dfrac{\tan x + \tan y}{1 - \tan x \tan y} = 1$

$\tan x + \tan y = 1 - \tan x \tan y$

$\tan x + \tan y + \tan x \tan y = 1$

Adding $1$ to both sides:

$1 + \tan x + \tan y + \tan x \tan y = 2$

$(1 + \tan x)(1 + \tan y) = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Given the following expression
A) $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{c}$
B) $\vec{a} \times (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})$
C) $\vec{a} \cdot (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})$
D) $|\vec{a}|(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})$
E) $(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) \times (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})$
Then which of the following is not correct
options: B, C and E are meaningless
A is meaningful but B is meaningless
questions.solution:
Expression A: $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ is a vector. The dot product of a vector with another vector $\vec{c}$ is a scalar. Thus, A is meaningful.

Expression B: $(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})$ is a scalar. The cross product is defined only between two vectors. Thus, B is meaningless.

Expression C: $(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})$ is a scalar. The dot product is defined only between two vectors. Thus, C is meaningless.

Expression D: $|\vec{a}|$ is a scalar and $(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})$ is a scalar. The product of two scalars is a scalar. Thus, D is meaningful.

Expression E: $(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})$ and $(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})$ are both scalars. The cross product is defined only between two vectors. Thus, E is meaningless.

From the above analysis, A and D are meaningful, while B, C, and E are meaningless.

The statement "B and E are meaningful" is incorrect.

Answer: B and E are meaningful

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The volume of the parallelopiped whose coterminous edges are $2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}, 3\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}, \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ is
questions.solution:
Let the coterminous edges be $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = 3\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}$, and $\vec{c} = \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$.

The volume of the parallelopiped is given by the absolute value of the scalar triple product $[\vec{a} \ \vec{b} \ \vec{c}]$.

$[\vec{a} \ \vec{b} \ \vec{c}] = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \end{vmatrix}$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:

$[\vec{a} \ \vec{b} \ \vec{c}] = 2(-3 + 1) - 1(9 - 0) - 1(3 - 0)$

$[\vec{a} \ \vec{b} \ \vec{c}] = -4 - 9 - 3 = -16$

$V = |-16| = 16$ cu. units.

Answer: $16$ cu. units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are three non-coplanar vectors and $\vec{p}, \vec{q}, \vec{r}$ are defined as $\vec{p} = \dfrac{\vec{b} \times \vec{c}}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}, \vec{q} = \dfrac{\vec{c} \times \vec{a}}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}, \vec{r} = \dfrac{\vec{a} \times \vec{b}}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}$, then $[(\vec{a} + \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{p} + (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) \cdot \vec{q} + (\vec{c} + \vec{a}) \cdot \vec{r}]$ is equal to
questions.solution:
The given vectors $\vec{p}, \vec{q}, \vec{r}$ are the reciprocal vectors of $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$.

Using the properties of reciprocal vectors, we have:
$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{p} = \dfrac{\vec{a} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} = \dfrac{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} = 1$
$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{p} = \dfrac{\vec{b} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} = 0$

Similarly, for the other dot products:
$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{q} = 1$, $\vec{c} \cdot \vec{q} = 0$
$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{r} = 1$, $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{r} = 0$

Expanding the given expression:
$(\vec{a} + \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{p} + (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) \cdot \vec{q} + (\vec{c} + \vec{a}) \cdot \vec{r}$

$= (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{p} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{p}) + (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{q} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{q}) + (\vec{c} \cdot \vec{r} + \vec{a} \cdot \vec{r})$

Substituting the values obtained above:
$= (1 + 0) + (1 + 0) + (1 + 0)$

$= 1 + 1 + 1 = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\vec{u} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}, \vec{v} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{w}$ is unit vector then the maximum value of scalar triple product $[\vec{u}\ \vec{v}\ \vec{w}]$ is
questions.solution:
The scalar triple product is given by $[\vec{u}\ \vec{v}\ \vec{w}] = (\vec{u} \times \vec{v}) \cdot \vec{w}$.

First, we find the cross product $\vec{u} \times \vec{v}$:

$\vec{u} \times \vec{v} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{u} \times \vec{v} = \hat{i}(2 - 0) - \hat{j}(1 - (-4)) + \hat{k}(0 - 4)$

$\vec{u} \times \vec{v} = 2\hat{i} - 5\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$

The magnitude of this vector is:

$|\vec{u} \times \vec{v}| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-5)^2 + (-4)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 25 + 16} = \sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5}$

The dot product $(\vec{u} \times \vec{v}) \cdot \vec{w}$ is maximized when the unit vector $\vec{w}$ is in the same direction as $\vec{u} \times \vec{v}$.

Maximum value $= |\vec{u} \times \vec{v}| |\vec{w}| \cos(0^{\circ})$

Since $|\vec{w}| = 1$, the maximum value is $3\sqrt{5} \times 1 \times 1 = 3\sqrt{5}$.

Answer: $3\sqrt{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{k}, \vec{b} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, and $\vec{c} = 4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$. If $\vec{r}$ is a vector such that $\vec{r} \times \vec{b} = \vec{c} \times \vec{b}$ and $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$, Then $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{c} =$
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{r} \times \vec{b} = \vec{c} \times \vec{b}$

$(\vec{r} - \vec{c}) \times \vec{b} = 0$

$\vec{r} - \vec{c} = \lambda \vec{b}$

$\vec{r} = \vec{c} + \lambda \vec{b}$

Taking the dot product with $\vec{a}$:

$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} + \lambda (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}) = 0$

Calculating the dot products:

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = (4)(2) + (-3)(0) + (7)(1) = 15$

$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} = (1)(2) + (1)(0) + (1)(1) = 3$

Substituting these values:

$15 + 3\lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = -5$

Thus, $\vec{r} = \vec{c} - 5\vec{b}$

$\vec{r} = (4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}) - 5(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = -\hat{i} - 8\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

Now, calculating $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{c}$:

$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{c} = (-\hat{i} - 8\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) \cdot (4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k})$

$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{c} = -4 + 24 + 14 = 34$

Answer: $34$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A current of 4 A is flowing at 230 V in the primary coil of a transformer. If the voltage produced in the secondary coil is 2300 V and 40 % of power is lost, then the current in the secondary will be
questions.solution:
Power in primary coil, $P_p = V_p I_p$

$P_p = 230 \times 4 = 920$ W
